summary:
The scanner change works on this PC's live container layer. I tested it on the current boot (2026-10-04T19:11Z, the spike #87 fresh boot), after first confirming the layer is still armable:
- Opening 3 layer files for read added +3 WCsc/WCfc/WCri and +3 System 0x120089 handles.
- The app's own Scanner, with the store rule switched off through the test seam (reflection probe in .taad-scratch), walked Files\Windows\Globalization 4 times. Every walk added +5 WCsc/WCfc/WCri/FMwi and +5 System handles, and idle windows freed none of it.
- Against that, the published exe gave 0 on every WC* tag and 0 System handles: X-001 refusing the real store in 3 spellings, and X-002 scanning ...\Containers (skippedStores 1, opensUnderExcludedStore 0).
- The full suite, including the repro and the 32 ContainerLayerStoreTests, also gave 0 WC*.

Other gates:
- Full suite: 532 passed. The same 3 last-access tests that were failing before this slice still fail.
- X-005, X-006 and T-003 passed. PoolWatchCases C-052 to C-056 passed; the rehearsal read RUN COMPLETE.
- WindowMutants -Mutant All: all 11 mutants were caught (Q-114).
- Fitness: 81 rules hold. The rules harness (Q-027): 93/93 AS-RECORDED at engine 3e58aae.

The verdict is partial, for these reasons:
1. **Criterion 7 does not meet Q-186.** Q-186 was answered after the build and outranks critique F1. It says turning the checkbox off lifts the C: exclusion AND the picked-root refusal. The build keeps the refusal unconditional:
   - ContainerLayerStore.Resolve:95 turns only Exclude into None.
   - KnownWorkarounds.IfTurnedOff and MainWindow.xaml.cs:503 tell the user the refusal "does not depend on this setting".
   - X-005 and X-006 assert that wording.
2. **A loopback admin share reaches the store unmatched.** \\localhost\C$ (and \\127.0.0.1\C$) is readable by this unelevated user. The published exe given \\localhost\C$\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers\<id>\Files\Windows\Media did not refuse it: status Completed, 95 files, 14 folders read from inside the store. So the preconditions behind O-049 and O-084 are false on this PC, and Q-182's assumption that other spellings are caught does not hold for this one. That walk itself added 0 WC* for that folder.
3. **The leak is not first-touch only.** The app's own probe path leaked again on every repeat walk of the same subtree, contradicting the investigation's "repeat scan left 0". The user-facing texts (KnownWorkarounds.cs:29,38,46) say kernel memory is kept only for entries "read for the first time since the PC was restarted". That understates what turning the precaution off costs: repeated scans keep adding to it, which fits the report's "built up scan after scan". The 5 leaking entries are probably the non-Offline ReparsePoint+Sparse files under ICU, which SizeProbe opens.
4. **Fix obligations O-105 to O-109, owed to build-slice, are not done in the tree:**
   - -Report still does not read <RunDir>\fltmc.txt.
   - No fltmc fixtures exist.
   - The rule texts still name ScanArm (fitness.yaml lines 987, 996, 1018).
   - Read-Jsonl has no try/catch.
   - Invoke-ExeArm has no try/finally.
   O-014, O-041 and O-063 ask for verdict shapes (-Diff UNDECIDED, VOID) that the narrowed PoolWatch no longer has, so they look stale.
5. **O-002 is false:** the store holds real bytes outside any host projection, for example dotnet.bcf at 557,268 B. Q-180 and Q-181 already accept this, and the store is labelled 'size not counted'.

Not done here: the person-run Restart session (-Prepare/-Protocol), a whole-C: scan, and `fltmc filters`.

Side observation for SC-128: the full suite pushed paged pool up by about 143 MB (FMfn +145K live), and it was reclaimed within about 2 minutes with no memory pressure.

My run's total: WC* +23, all from the stated, bounded positive controls; the paged pool counter ended +9 MB above my first reading.

Loop note: build attempts 3–5 changed only PoolWatch, sent back by obligations with no src change. That loop shape is already recorded by the build stage.

obligations.evidence: The precondition is false. The store holds real files that are not projections of host files: Layers\<id>\dotnet.bcf 557,268 B, Specialization\config.json 664 B, Bindings\config.json 26 B (one-level metadata listing; WC* +0 for that listing). Files also holds ReparsePoint+Sparse files that are not Offline (ICU\icudtl.dat, *.res). Skipping the store therefore loses bytes. Q-180 and Q-181 already accept this as a labelled 'size not counted' shortfall, and the build shows it that way (X-006: core.notScanned 1).

Another path does reach the store's contents. \\localhost\C$ and \\127.0.0.1\C$ are readable by this unelevated user. Given \\localhost\C$\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers\1f35079a-...\Files\Windows\Media, the published exe returned exit 0, status Completed, 95 files, 14 folders, with no refusal and no skipped store. ContainerLayerStore.cs:58-59 already says loopback SMB is 'not covered, and not looked for'. No other WCI store was found: C:\ProgramData\Docker\windowsfilter is absent.

On this boot the layer is armable on the app's own path: Scanner.Scan with the store rule off leaked +5 WCsc/WCfc/WCri and +5 System 0x120089 handles on every walk of Files\Windows\Globalization (n=4). The published exe scanning ...\Containers (X-002, which lists BaseImages, ContainerStorages, Dumps and Snapshots and skips Layers) gave WC* +0 and System 0x120089 +0. So did the full suite, which includes the repro scanning the real Containers folder. Spike #87's fresh-boot walk past Containers also showed no WC* rise.

A root spelled through the loopback admin share (\\localhost\C$\ProgramData\...\Layers\<id>\Files\Windows\Media) is not matched. The published exe scanned it (Completed, 95 files, 14 folders) instead of refusing it as Q-182 requires. The share is reachable unelevated on this PC. Whether this walk leaks server-side for the entries that leak locally was not tried: the Media folder gave WC* +0.

No test feeds 'the pool protocol against a boot that already walked the layer' (C-011). The narrowed PoolWatch has no VOID or armability judgement left to feed it, so this obligation looks stale against design 10. It is owed to build-slice.

There is no -Diff, no PASS/UNDECIDED verdict and no burst-gap drift in the narrowed PoolWatch.ps1. The shape it asks for (C-027) does not exist in the tree; this looks stale against design 10. Owed to build-slice.
There is no closing-layer-control VOID in the narrowed PoolWatch.ps1. The C-041 shape is not fed by any case; this looks stale against design 10. Owed to build-slice.

Not fixed. PoolWatch.ps1:272 reads only $pasteDir\fltmc.txt inside Get-EnvironmentRecord, Write-RunReport reads no fltmc.txt, and the header (:22) still says '<RunDir>\fltmc.txt (or the prepare folder's)'.
Not fixed. Select-String finds 0 'Filter Name' or 0x80070005 fixtures in tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1. The C-052 rehearsal printed 'FILTERS UNDECIDED: not supplied' only.

Not fixed. .taad/fitness.yaml:987 'the tolerance verdict judged by it'; :996 'lives in tests/window/ScanArm'; :1018-1020 'ScanArm has InternalsVisibleTo into Core ... voids the protocol's WC* clause'.
Not fixed. PoolWatch.ps1:382 Read-Jsonl still pipes every non-blank line into ConvertFrom-Json under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop', with no try/catch and no NUL trim.
Not fixed. Invoke-ExeArm has only `try { $p.Kill() } catch { }` (:352). There is no try/finally around the poll loop, and :397 still reports a missing arm line as 'never started'.

Q-186, answered after build attempt 6 and outranking critique F1, says the 'wcifs-layer-store' off position lifts BOTH the C: exclusion and the picked-root refusal for that session. The tree implements F1 instead:
- ContainerLayerStore.Resolve:95 maps only Exclude to None, so Refuse stays.
- KnownWorkarounds.cs:47-48 IfTurnedOff says 'A folder picked at or inside the store is still not scanned: that does not depend on this setting'.
- MainWindow.xaml.cs:503 says 'A folder at or inside the store is never scanned'.
- C-049's test asserts 'still Refused'.
- X-005 and X-006 pin that wording.
Criterion 7 is therefore unmet. Architecture edit AA-015's 'whatever the settings say' would also become false.

Measured this boot: the app's own Scanner (store rule off via the ContainerLayerStorePath='' seam) over the live layer's Files\Windows\Globalization added +5 WCsc/WCfc/WCri and +5 System 0x120089 handles on EACH of 4 consecutive walks, and none came back in the 30 s and 60 s idle windows (marks L0..N3 in .taad-scratch/validate/marks.jsonl). The user-facing texts say memory is kept only for entries 'read for the first time since the PC was restarted' (KnownWorkarounds.cs:29, :38, :46, shown in X-005's confirmation and X-006's notes). That understates what turning the precaution off costs: every scan leaks again. The design record's first-touch claim, taken from the investigation's 'repeat scan left 0', needs the same correction.

Q-182 assumes that 'subst, junction or \\?\ forms of the path are caught too'. On this PC the unelevated user can read \\localhost\C$ and \\127.0.0.1\C$, and the published exe scanned a folder inside the store through that spelling (Completed, 95 files, 14 folders, no refusal). A C: scan started at \\localhost\C$\ would likewise not exclude the store. The design scoped this out ('not covered, and not looked for'). Whether Resolve must map local admin-share roots, and so whether O-049/O-084 can be met, is a design decision.
